package_info.why_malicious: The package exposes an exported activity (TagViewer) that can be triggered by any app without permissions. This allows a malicious app to simulate NFC tag scans and present arbitrary, attacker-controlled content to the user via a trusted system UI, enabling phishing, social engineering, or other attacks without user awareness or consent.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a malicious app chooses to execute the attack logic
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app code (not in com.android.apps.tag, but abuses its exported activity)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code constructs a fake NDEF message containing a malicious URL, creates an explicit Intent targeting the exported TagViewer activity in com.android.apps.tag, injects the crafted NDEF message as extra data, and launches the activity, resulting in the system displaying a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-controlled content.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: This code enables any app to simulate an NFC tag scan and present arbitrary content to the user through a trusted system UI, bypassing the need for actual NFC hardware or user interaction. This can be used to deceive users into interacting with malicious content.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normally, only genuine NFC tag scans should trigger the TagViewer activity, and only with data from real, physical tags. Here, any app can trigger the system UI with arbitrary, attacker-supplied data, violating the user's expectation of authenticity and security.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may use NFC intents for genuine tag reading and processing, but should not spoof tags or trigger system UIs with fabricated data without user action.
key_indicators: Explicit invocation of com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted NDEF messages
No permissions required to trigger sensitive system UI
Ability to inject arbitrary NDEF messages into system activity
startActivity call targeting system NFC tag viewer

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when the user scans a real NFC tag and the malicious app is installed and receives the intent
execution_context.file_location: Malicious app code (AndroidManifest.xml intent filter for ACTION_NDEF_DISCOVERED and corresponding app code)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, when a real NFC tag is scanned, the malicious app intercepts the NFC intent via a high-priority intent filter, parses the genuine tag data, replaces it with attacker-controlled content (such as a malicious phone number), and forwards the modified NDEF message to the TagViewer activity, causing the system UI to display spoofed information instead of the real tag data.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Intercepting and modifying NFC tag data before it reaches the system UI allows the attacker to present falsified information to the user, enabling phishing, fraud, or social engineering attacks by abusing the trust in the system UI.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Users expect the system UI to display the authentic content of scanned NFC tags. This attack breaks that trust by substituting attacker-controlled data, making the user vulnerable to deception.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate apps may process NFC tags for their own functionality, but should not alter and forward modified data to system UIs as if it were genuine tag content.
key_indicators: Intent filter for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED in AndroidManifest.xml
Modification of NFC tag data in app code before forwarding
Forwarding spoofed NDEF messages to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer
startActivity call with crafted NDEF message after intercepting real tag

attack_chain.action: Malicious app registers for NFC intents (e.g., ACTION_NDEF_DISCOVERED) to intercept tag scans or directly crafts and sends explicit intents to TagViewer with attacker-controlled data.
attack_chain.leads_to: User is presented with attacker-controlled content in the trusted system UI, simulating a legitimate NFC tag scan.

attack_chain.action: User sees a 'new tag scanned' popup with attacker-supplied data, such as a malicious URL or phone number, displayed by the system UI.
attack_chain.leads_to: User may interact with the attacker-controlled content, believing it to be authentic tag data.

attack_chain.action: If the user clicks the link or initiates a call, the attacker's payload is executed (e.g., browser opens a phishing site, call is placed to an attacker-controlled number).
attack_chain.leads_to: Final goal: user compromise, credential theft, phishing, or social engineering.

behavioral_signatures: Apps sending explicit intents to com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer with crafted or non-genuine NDEF messages
Apps registering for android.nfc.action.NDEF_DISCOVERED and modifying tag data before forwarding to system activities
Unexpected 'new tag scanned' popups in the system UI without corresponding NFC hardware activity
startActivity calls targeting com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer from non-system apps
file_indicators: App code invoking startActivity with com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer as the explicit target
Presence of NdefMessage.createUri with suspicious or hardcoded URLs or phone numbers
network_indicators: NDEF messages containing URLs to suspicious or known phishing domains (e.g., kripthor.com/nfc)
NDEF messages with phone numbers not matching expected tag content (e.g., tel:666-666-666)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for apps that register for high-priority NFC intents and forward modified NDEF messages to system activities, especially com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer. Flag apps that invoke startActivity with com.android.apps.tag.TagViewer as the target and supply crafted NDEF data, particularly when no actual NFC hardware event is detected. Alert on repeated 'new tag scanned' popups without corresponding NFC activity, or on NDEF messages containing known malicious URLs or phone numbers. Correlate app behavior with system logs to identify unauthorized invocation of TagViewer.
